submissions.findingTextShort: A 2026 uncontrolled Petamig real-world study reported within-person migraine improvements but cannot establish randomized efficacy.
submissions.findingTextNormalized: A 2026 real-world study followed 120 migraine patients using the proprietary Petamig butterbur preparation and reported favorable within-person outcomes. With no randomized control group, the study is supportive observational context only and should not upgrade efficacy certainty above controlled evidence.
submissions.populationContext: 120 migraine patients in an uncontrolled real-world study.
submissions.uncertaintyNote: No control group; proprietary product identity must remain explicit.

submissions.findingTextShort: Butterbur safety is preparation-dependent; pyrrolizidine-alkaloid exposure makes verified PA-free product identity essential.
submissions.findingTextNormalized: Hepatobiliary and toxicological evidence on butterbur extracts reinforces that pyrrolizidine-alkaloid content and extract preparation are safety-critical. Only specifically verified PA-free products can inherit consumer-facing safety or efficacy claims; raw or unverified butterbur must not be treated as equivalent.
submissions.safetyContext: PA contamination can create serious toxicity concerns; verified PA-free identity is a prerequisite.
submissions.uncertaintyNote: This source is toxicological rather than direct randomized efficacy evidence; keep safety and efficacy evidence classes separate.

submissions.findingTextShort: A meta-analysis of randomized cycling time-trial evidence provides exercise-specific sodium-bicarbonate efficacy context rather than a universal performance claim.
submissions.findingTextNormalized: Randomized cycling time-trial evidence synthesized in a systematic review and meta-analysis supports a possible ergogenic effect of sodium bicarbonate in defined exercise contexts. Exercise modality, dose, timing, sodium load, and gastrointestinal tolerance are proposition-critical and the result should not be generalized to all athletes or performance tasks.
submissions.usageContext: Acute sodium-bicarbonate exercise supplementation; modality, timing, and dose specific.
submissions.safetyContext: GI intolerance, sodium load, and acid-base, renal, and cardiovascular context require separate safety handling.
submissions.uncertaintyNote: Performance effects are context-specific and should not become a universal ergogenic claim.

submissions.findingTextShort: PMID 12612144 is a processed-tomato/lycopene trial and cannot support Chromium glucose-control efficacy.
submissions.findingTextNormalized: The current Chromium glucose-control claim cites PMID 12612144, a trial of processed tomato products and plasma lycopene concentrations. Chromium was not the tested intervention, so the source is semantically invalid for the claim and must be quarantined before evidence grading.

submissions.findingTextShort: A randomized-trial meta-analysis of Chromium found glycemic effects with very high heterogeneity, requiring form and baseline-status boundaries.
submissions.findingTextNormalized: A systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized chromium trials reported pooled glycemic changes but substantial to very high heterogeneity across outcomes. Chromium picolinate, yeast, chloride, nicotinate and other forms, doses, durations, and baseline glycemic states should not be pooled into one consumer efficacy sentence.
submissions.uncertaintyNote: High heterogeneity and formulation variation materially limit universal glucose-control conclusions.
